title: Lesson 74: The Security Review: A Full Threat Model for an Agent System
description: How to run a security review and build a full threat model for an agent: start with assets and never-boundaries, map the trust boundaries in the agent's chain, run a defined threat set (prompt injection, tool misuse, excessive agency, data exfiltration), tier by impact, and write down the residual risk a named owner accepts.

questions.question: Why does an agent security review start by naming assets and never-boundaries before listing attacks?
options: Because the attack list is identical for every agent and needs no local context to apply
Because you cannot decide what to defend against until you have named what a threat is meant to reach
Because threat modeling only ever cares about the confidentiality of stored customer records and nothing else
Because naming assets matters only for auditors after launch, not for the design itself
questions.explanation: You cannot harden against a threat until you know what it is trying to reach. Naming assets and the action the system must never take gives each threat something concrete to attach to.

questions.question: An injected instruction convinces the model to request a sensitive action. What actually prevents the action?
options: The model's safety training recognizes the injected text and refuses to proceed with the requested call
The retrieved document is validated and removed before it can enter the context window
A deterministic boundary the model cannot override makes the action unachievable from where it sits
The prompt is compared against a known-good hash and replaced whenever it has changed
questions.explanation: An injection targets the model, so moving its intent is not the same as moving the action. The defense lives in deterministic boundaries, such as permission limits and verify steps, that the model cannot talk its way past.

questions.question: What is the most important property of the residual-risk record in a written security review?
options: Every accepted risk carries a named owner and a reason, so it is a decision, not an omission
Every threat is fully mitigated so that no residual risk remains anywhere in the reviewed system
Residual risk is recorded only for threats that exceed a fixed token-spend threshold set by finance
The column is populated automatically by the vendor's security scanning tool at deployment time
questions.explanation: No agent is fully hardened, so the review must record which remaining risks were knowingly accepted and by whom. An accepted risk with a name and a reason is a decision; without one it is just an omission.
